mechanism_narrative: A persistently high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4%) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, and since UNRATE has historically exceeded 4% in most periods, the signal is always active without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4%, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5%), the Federal Reserve's expected policy tightening leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp unemployment rate increase (UNRATE > 8%) signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial contraction (INDPRO < 90) indicates weakening manufacturing output, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 90, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 90) signals economic slowdown, associated with negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through prolonged corporate earnings pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 90 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through increased real interest rates.
failure_condition: The joint rise in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances over a 3-year rolling window.
